Author: Sanjay Kumar
Bench: Sanjay Kumar
 1
 In The Supreme Court Of India
 Civil Appellate Jurisdiction
 Civil Appeal No. /2025

(@ SLP (C) No. 5541/2020)
 KARNAVATI SALES CORPORATION & ORS. APPELLANT(

VERSUS  AHMEDABAD MUNICIPAL CORPORATION & RESPONDENT(
 ANR.
O R D E R Leave granted.

Mr. Sanjay Kumar Pathak, learned counsel, appearing for the appellants, states that the present appeal does not survive for consideration on merits as the appellant Nos. 1, 3 and 4 are not in existence anymore and appellant No. 2, Hajarbhai Surajmal Pannalal, expired.

Appellant No. 1, Karnavati Sales Corporation, is a sole proprietorship and its proprietor, namely,
Kanaiyalal Pannalal, is stated to have expired on 21.01.2023.
Appellant No. 2, Hajarbhai Surajmal Pannalal, is stated to have expired on 29.04.2021, while, Savarmal Sainee, the nominee of Kuber Tobacco Products Pvt. Ltd., appellant No. 3, expired on 30.04.2021.

It is further stated that Kuber Tobacco Products Pvt. Ltd., which is shown independently as appellant No. 4, closed down in 2009 and surrendered its license under the Prevention of Food Adulteration Act, 1954.

In the light of aforestated developments and as appellant Nos. 1, 2 and 3, namely, the proprietor of Karnavati Sales Corporation, Hajarbhai Surajmal Pannalal and the nominee of Kuber Tobacco Products Pvt. Ltd.,
were sentenced by the High Court to suffer imprisonment, which direction is now rendered incapable of execution owing to their expiry, the matter requires to be closed.

As regards Kuber Tobacco Product Pvt. Ltd, appellant No. 4, the High Court imposed a fine of 25,000/- (Rupees Karnavati Sales Corporation vs Ahmedabad Municipal Corporation on 21 May, 2025 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/186320959/
1 twenty five thousand only) upon it, but as the said company is stated to have closed down as long back as in the year 2009, we see no purpose in considering the validity of such imposition on merits at this stage.
